description: We are 2 CIS students from Wilbur Wright College of City Colleges of Chicago. We're ready for a challenge and excited to learn.
summary: Utilizing the NASA FIRMS data our project combines data from 2 sensors reporting on fires and burning activity on earth and then provides a user-friendly interface to access that data fast and efficiently.
details:
We requested the fire activity data from the NASA FIRMS database for the 2 MODIS and VIIRS sensors from the early 2000s to the current month of November 2026. With that created a web interface using html and php for the target audience like emergency responders and scientists to be able to access historical data about fires and burning activity quickly and efficiently. They are able to search for fire activity in a specific area for a specific time range coming from the combined sensor data and see an overview of the most important statistical data they can then download as a csv file to work with further.

Given the complicated process and huge amount of csv files we only used archived data for the US and Canada to harmonize and populate the interface. For the future we would want to take the time to process and utilize data from the entire earth.

Using python libraries, we would take all the data we've collected to start streaming every file into a . parquet file. The program would the divide each cell into a db to then begin the harmonization process of 3 different senors, two of the same type, the MODIS sensor and two VIIRS sensors (since one sensor was replaced around 2012). Using python the program will parse through all the data and start harmonizing it all in a dst/src ratio. From that we use PHP to create the front end, connecting the pipeline and PHP using Flask in an application.py file. We would then use leaflet to generate a map to populate it with all of the data we have collected. Using our cloud knowledge with AWS we deployed our project on Elastic Beanstalk using Docker.

For full transperency, as CIS students from community college, we had a different expectation of what was expected of us, so we went into this focusing heavily on the backend and code of it. We utilized SI as little as possible, which led to us not being able to get a full and working product/solution in time. We underestimated the scale of this challenge and how heavily it relied on the use of SI.

For us, it was simply not possible to submit a finished project in time, despite being at the local event in Chicago 7am-8:30pm Saturday and 7am-6pm Sunday, which is why most of the functionality is not implemented. We still enjoyed the hackathon and would've loved to it over a longer period of time and fully brood over the challenge at a bigger scale.
